phase.title: CLI and dual-view Web UI for the Agent Harness
phase.goal: Provide a fast operational CLI and one local Web UI with Simple and Detailed views, driven exclusively by the Phase 4 RPC API.

implementation_evidence.offline: 137 pytest tests passed, including 12 Node JavaScript contract tests and CLI process/socket integration.
implementation_evidence.checks: Ruff and Mypy clean; wheel and sdist build with packaged web assets.
implementation_evidence.remaining: Manual browser visual/keyboard checks and separate live-provider demonstration through the new clients. No paid model calls made during this implementation.

approved_scope_update.cli: Interactive commands and one-shot operations for quick control, watching, JSON inspection and scripting.
approved_scope_update.web: One local web application: Simple for task/progress/result, Detailed for trace, usage, tool attempts, JSON and architecture explanation.
approved_scope_update.mode_toggle: Presentation only; never submit, cancel, restart or change the selected run. Remember only a device-local view preference. Not an authorization boundary.
approved_scope_update.implementation: Reuse rpc_client.py and progress.py. Serve packaged HTML/CSS/JS alongside /rpc. No new frontend framework, public deployment or agent loop. The approved session-picker extension adds a read-only RPC and two SQLite lookup indexes.
approved_scope_update.session_picker: Replace the Web paste-ID input with a scrollable server-backed dropdown: 20 summaries per page, newest-created first, title from first task, timestamp and latest run status. Selection opens the session/latest run without replay or cancellation; preserve selection on loading failure. CLI keeps its ID commands.
approved_scope_update.live_validation: Phase 4 live evidence is not proof of these new clients. New paid requests require a separate explicit demo run.

placement_policy.decision: Implement after Phase 4 and before the Phase 5 test-support bonus. Keep existing phase numbers and acceptance IDs unchanged.
placement_policy.reason: The finished interface depends on Phase 4 RPC operations and JSON responses. Building it first against AgentService directly would introduce a second integration path and would not demonstrate platform control over RPC.
placement_policy.early_work: Command design and pure rendering fixtures can be prepared before Phase 4, but completion requires the real RPC transport and end-to-end checks.
placement_policy.assessment_scope: CLI and Web UI are chosen demo aids, not additional mandatory deliverables. Phase 4 remains independently demonstrable and Phase 5 does not require these optional clients.

mapping.requirement: Create/manage sessions, send tasks and inspect runs over a thin RPC API.
mapping.interface_behavior: Create a session or attach by known session ID; submit a task; inspect a run by ID. All operations go through Phase 4 RPC.

mapping.requirement: Demonstrate a task end to end with visible reasoning and tool calls, then cancel an active run.
mapping.interface_behavior: Show model-step progress, requested tool names/arguments, results/errors and final output; provide a responsive cancel command while watching. Reasoning visibility uses execution progress and any available public explanation, never private chain-of-thought or fabricated internal thoughts.

mapping.requirement: Explain tool failure, unknown tools and slow/disconnected servers.
mapping.interface_behavior: Render existing structured errors and attempt metadata. Use controlled Phase 4 fixtures to demonstrate failure; the client does not invent failure behavior.

mapping.requirement: Persist and resume sessions; store every tool call/event for traceability.
mapping.interface_behavior: Reattach to known session/run IDs, page through persisted events and submit a follow-up as a new run. The server remains the history source.

mapping.requirement: Build the runtime yourself and explain boundaries; one real LLM provider is sufficient.
mapping.interface_behavior: Reuse AgentService, AgentHarness, AgentLoop, MCP and persistence through RPC. Provider configuration and tool execution remain server responsibilities.

entry_condition: Phase 4 exposes and verifies create_session, get_session, submit_task, get_run, list_run_events and cancel_run. Its JSON envelopes, event cursor and cancellation behavior are documented.
implementation_guidelines: Use Python/uv for CLI and packaged HTML/CSS/JavaScript for Web; a full-screen TUI or frontend framework is not required.
Reuse the Phase 4 transport client or extract a small shared client if the demo already has one. Reuse existing event-rendering logic where compatible with the public JSON contract.
Keep request handling, event presentation and interaction coordination in a few focused modules. Do not build a generic UI/plugin framework.
Support command input while event polling is active; avoid blocking the event loop with input() or sharing a synchronous request lock that prevents cancel.
Keep server responses authoritative. Treat tool output as display data, escape terminal control sequences and never execute returned text.
Preserve existing event names and JSON envelopes. Do not export private _message fields or raw SDK internals just to make the display richer.
in_scope: Connect to the transport selected in Phase 4 with documented local configuration.
Create a session, attach to a known session ID, submit a task and show the returned run ID immediately.
Inspect/watch a known run, showing persisted status, progress events, tool calls, results/errors and final output.
Cancel the watched or explicitly selected run while it is active and show the acknowledged server state.
Page through a previous run's trace and reattach after client or server restart.
Provide readable default output plus an explicit JSON inspection mode using existing public responses.
Document a short assessment demo and add focused client behavior/contract tests.
Build a local Web UI with Simple/Detailed views using existing HTTP RPC operations.
Add architecture explanation, grouped tool attempts and public JSON inspection to Detailed view.
out_of_scope: Product chat features, voice input/output, full-screen terminal UI, public hosting or a separate frontend application stack
New agent loops, direct database access, direct MCP calls or direct LLM calls from the interface
New provider configuration UI, model switching, automatic provider fallback or token/cost estimates invented by the client
Run listing or session/run search endpoints, editing/deleting history and operator reconciliation controls (bounded session listing is now approved)
New runtime retry policies, automatic task resubmission, automatic replay of interrupted tools or submit-task idempotency infrastructure
Authentication systems, hosted deployments, multi-user tenancy or OS sandboxing

architecture.flow: CLI or Web UI -> HTTP RPC -> AgentService -> AgentHarness/AgentLoop -> LLMProvider and MCPToolExecutor; the service/store persist state and events.
architecture.client_owns: Input validation, RPC request mapping, selected IDs, per-run display cursor, bounded local polling and rendering.
architecture.server_owns: Admission, task execution, lifecycle, cancellation, retries, budgets, tool permissions, persistence and recovery.
architecture.reuse: Existing core/debug.py is a presentation reference/helper, not a reason to import AgentService or open SQLite in the client. Adapt only the public event shape; share a pure renderer if useful.
architecture.transport: HTTP RPC on the existing local server. Web assets use the same origin. Client exit stops observation only; the separate server and accepted runs remain alive.

detailed: Architecture map linked to selected event
web_contract.architecture_map: HTML/SVG pipeline with separate provider/LLM and MCP/tool branches, return arrows to the loop and an audit storage link. Follow latest received event or explicitly pin a historical event; pause/disconnect labels remain honest. Click nodes for responsibilities and related events. No profiler, private reasoning, added RPC or graph framework.
web_contract.safety: Render data as text. Credentials stay server-side. Mode selection is not role-based access control.
web_contract.bounds: Bound rendering/page sizes, disclose omitted old display entries and offer paged server history.
web_contract.interaction: Input/cancel remain responsive during polling. Old watch responses cannot overwrite a newly selected run.
web_contract.no_resubmission: Ambiguous submit/cancel outcomes are unconfirmed; never automatically repeat a mutation.

interaction_contract.layout: A simple header shows connection status, selected session/run IDs and last confirmed run status. An append-only event feed shows sequence, type and a short payload summary. A prompt accepts commands during watch mode.

commands.behavior: Create and display a session ID. Do not automatically resend if the response is lost.
Verify and select an existing session. A known ID is sufficient; no new listing API is required.
Submit once to the selected session, show returned run ID/status, then start watching. Keep input available for cancellation. A conflict leaves the existing run unchanged.
Display the authoritative lightweight snapshot, usage, error and output when present.
Observe the run using its own cursor. Stop any previous watch before switching.
Use the explicit or watched run ID; send an idempotent cancel request independently of the polling loop.
Read paginated history without advancing another run's watch cursor; allow readable or JSON output.
Stop local observation. The client sends no cancellation request.
Show command help or close client-owned resources; explain server lifetime for the selected transport. Quit is not reported as a confirmed run cancellation.

interaction_contract.json_mode: An explicit output option prints public RPC JSON responses/event pages without colors or terminal decorations. Human prompts/connection notices must not corrupt machine-readable stdout.
interaction_contract.large_payloads: Readable summaries may truncate long payloads with an explicit indicator. JSON inspection preserves the public value; never write truncated values back to the server.
interaction_contract.availability: Missing provider/model/token metadata is omitted or shown as unavailable. A connection problem is a client observation, not a fabricated failed/cancelled run status.

observation_policy.polling: Default to incremental polling of list_run_events with after_sequence and bounded page size. A configurable interval around 500 ms is sufficient; reuse Phase 4 streaming only if it is already available and simpler.
observation_policy.ordering: Maintain a cursor per watched run; render ascending sequence values once during an attachment. Advance only after accepting the page. Follow has_more to drain backlog with yielding so command input remains responsive.
observation_policy.terminal: After get_run confirms a terminal status, drain persisted event pages to has_more=false before stopping watch, so the terminal event/final output is not missed. Use the terminal snapshot as authoritative.
observation_policy.disconnect: Show disconnected and last confirmed state. Stop automatic polling on transport failure and allow explicit watch/reattach to resume from the last cursor; bound every client request.
observation_policy.restart: Within one client process retain cursor by run ID. After client restart accept a supplied cursor or start at zero. Do not introduce a second durable event store.
observation_policy.lost_submission_response: If submit_task may have reached the server but no response was received, show outcome unconfirmed. Do not resend automatically or claim the run failed; document that recovering an unknown run ID is limited by Phase 4 lookup/idempotency support.
observation_policy.cancellation: Display cancel_requested until the server confirms a terminal state. If completion won the race, display completed. If cancel RPC fails, show unconfirmed and let the user inspect/retry; never claim the remote tool was rolled back.
observation_policy.client_exit: Release polling tasks and client-owned transport resources. Remote run continuation depends on transport/server ownership; any subsequent interrupted/cancelled state must come from the server.

demo_scenarios: Start the Phase 4 runtime and separate mock MCP server; connect the terminal client and create a session.
Submit a task that produces at least one MCP tool call, inspect ordered progress/tool results and the final answer. Use the real provider for the assessment demo.
Use a controlled Phase 4 failure fixture to display tool error/timeout or connection loss. Provider behavior may vary; deterministic tests use a clearly labeled fake.
Start a deliberately slow run, issue cancel while I/O is active, and observe persisted cancellation with no subsequent model/tool work.
Stop/restart or reattach according to the documented transport lifecycle, inspect the old run, then submit a follow-up in the same session as a new run.
Briefly demonstrate JSON inspection and explain that presentation, execution and durable state have separate owners.
suggested_files: src/minder_harness/cli.py and observation.py: terminal commands and cursor-based observation
src/minder_harness/web/: static UI and browser RPC client; web_routes.py: packaged same-origin assets
Phase 4 RPC client module: reuse public operation mapping and request timeouts
src/minder_harness/core/debug.py or a focused presentation helper: reuse compatible pure rendering
tests/test_terminal_client.py: command mapping, polling, cancellation and error behavior
pyproject.toml: CLI entry point only when implementation starts
docs/guides/interfaces.md: actual CLI/Web commands, transport lifetime, setup and demo

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A documented uv command starts the client, and session creation/attachment, task submission and status inspection all use actual Phase 4 RPC.
During an active run, the client displays ordered persisted model/tool events and accepts a cancel command without waiting for run completion.
Cancellation distinguishes request acknowledgment from terminal state, handles completion races, and never labels a failed cancel request as confirmed cancellation.
Watch handles multiple event pages, repeated pages and run switches without duplicate display or cursor mixing, and drains remaining events after terminal confirmation.
A disconnect preserves the last confirmed state/cursor, reattachment resumes inspection, and an ambiguous submit response never triggers automatic resubmission.
After documented client/server restart, known IDs allow trace inspection and session continuation as a new run with existing recovery semantics.
Tool failures and runtime limits appear as existing structured outcomes; long payloads have explicit truncation and terminal escape sequences are rendered safely.
Public JSON inspection is parseable and preserves values without presentation noise, secrets, SDK internals or private chain-of-thought.
Stopping watch/closing the client cleans up local tasks; server-lifetime behavior is documented and the client never invents a final run state.
Web modes share the selected run; toggling sends no mutation and preserves observation.
Detailed view groups attempt/logical tool events without implying duplicate executions; raw public events remain inspectable.
Static assets ship in the Python package, load from the local RPC origin and render external content as inert text.
CLI supports one-shot JSON and interactive cancellation; Web handles run switches, disconnects, completion races and paged history honestly.
Offline RPC/client tests and normal project checks pass. The real-provider demo has recorded execution status, and any skipped live run is reported honestly.

validation_plan: Test command-to-RPC mapping and empty/invalid input, not pixel-perfect terminal layouts.
Test watch with paginated/repeated events, terminal transitions, RPC timeout, reattachment and independently responsive cancel.
Test lost submit response without replay, cancel/completion race and partial-startup/client cleanup.
Run a deterministic integration scenario through the actual Phase 4 RPC transport with fake provider and separate mock MCP, reusing its fixtures.
Run uv run pytest, uv run ruff format --check ., uv run ruff check . and uv run mypy; manually verify command entry during watch in PowerShell.
Run the real-provider demo separately with explicit credentials and record what was actually demonstrated.
deliverables: Small terminal RPC client with readable and JSON inspection
One local Web UI with Simple/Detailed toggle, grouped trace and architecture explanation
Focused client tests and updated engineering journal
exit_condition: A reviewer can use CLI or either Web view through RPC to inspect/control runs, demonstrate cancellation/failure and continue sessions. Mode switching does not change execution; clients add no agent logic.
